summary: Pure IIFE-extraction refactor reviewed and approved. All three private methods (parseDoubleQuotedAttr, parseSingleQuotedAttr, parseUnquotedAttr) are verbatim lifts of their former IIFE bodies, placed immediately below parse_attr() in a logical grouping. The match expression dispatch is idiomatic PHP 8+ and correct. Post-dispatch whitespace normalisation and class-attribute trim remain in parse_attr() where they belong. The asymmetry in parseUnquotedAttr (no cursor advance) is deliberate and correct — copy_until() leaves the cursor on the terminating character which the outer loop reads next. No blocking issues. All four acceptance criteria confirmed by direct code inspection.

comments.note: The inherited // next inline comments on the char/pos advance lines inside parseDoubleQuotedAttr and parseSingleQuotedAttr are accurate but redundant — the pre-increment pattern is established convention throughout this file. Safe to drop in a future cleanup pass, but they cause no harm.

The three new private methods use camelCase (parseDoubleQuotedAttr etc.) while all other methods on Parser use snake_case. This is a deliberate, plan-sanctioned decision scoped to private helpers only. The public and protected API surface remains entirely snake_case, so there is no contract breakage. Worth noting in documentation so future contributors understand the mixed convention is intentional for this visibility tier.

parseUnquotedAttr is intentionally asymmetric: it does not advance the cursor before or after reading the value, unlike the two quoted variants. The correctness depends on copy_until(TOKEN_ATTR) leaving $this->char on the terminating character which the outer do-while loop in read_tag() checks. This implicit contract is not documented inline. A brief comment explaining why no advance is needed here would protect against a future developer 'fixing' it to match the quoted-method pattern.

No blocking issues found. Code is a clean, mechanical lift with correct behaviour, correct visibility, and correct placement. The refactor reduces cognitive load in parse_attr() without introducing any new state or branching complexity.
